issues.failure_explanation:
The text claims that under the Kruzhkov transform $v = (1 - e^{-\lambda u})/\lambda$, the time-dependent equation $u_t + \|
abla u\| = 0$ is equivalent to $v_t + \lambda v + \|
abla v\| = 0$. By the chain rule, $v_t = e^{-\lambda u} u_t$ and $
abla v = e^{-\lambda u} 
abla u$. Since both the time derivative and the spatial gradient term are positively homogeneous of degree 1, $v_t + \|
abla v\| = e^{-\lambda u}(u_t + \|
abla u\|)$. Therefore, $u_t + \|
abla u\| = 0$ transforms to $v_t + \|
abla v\| = 0$, not $v_t + \lambda v + \|
abla v\| = 0$. The claimed equivalence is false; for example, any constant solution $u(t,x) = c > 0$ satisfies $u_t + \|
abla u\| = 0$, but the corresponding $v(t,x) = (1-e^{-\lambda c})/\lambda > 0$ yields $v_t + \lambda v + \|
abla v\| = 1 - e^{-\lambda c} 
eq 0$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the claim that $u_t + \|\nabla u\| = 0 \iff v_t + \lambda v + \|\nabla v\| = 0$ and clarify that the Kruzhkov transform does not induce a linear zeroth-order damping term in the evolution equation.
issues.overall_effect: The motivation in Section 2.4 asserting that the Kruzhkov transform provides strong monotonicity $\lambda v$ in the time-dependent case is mathematically invalid. (Section 3 handles the time-dependent setting via the implicit time-derivative instead.)
issues.title: False claim of equivalence for time-dependent Eikonal equation under Kruzhkov transform
issues.why_classification: This claim appears only as a remark in Section 2.4 and is not used in the formal proofs of Section 3, which rely directly on the temporal discretization term $\frac{u^n - u^{n-1}}{\Delta t}$ to achieve monotonicity rather than Kruzhkov transformation.
